notes:
Summary: Emerging platform for developer CI + IDE copilot. Very focused on safe tool-calling for code agents (run tests, invoke linters, capture build logs) inside ephemeral sandboxes. Key ask: low-latency streaming for in-IDE feedback, model pinning per repo branch, and strong isolation for build/test execution.

Recent conversation snippets: "We need to be able to run unit tests and linters via the assistant but ensure zero outbound network from the sandbox — build artifacts must be hermetic and logs stored to our VPC S3" — CTO (Paraphrase).

Technical priorities: repo-scoped model version pinning, deterministic reruns of failed tests (replayable KV/inputs), function/tool call audit trail (who, when, what artifacts), incremental streaming of test output into the IDE, and ability to route to smaller quantized models for linting vs larger models for code generation.

Cost/volume notes: expect heavy token volume during CI bursts (100s of concurrent sandboxed sessions per cluster); cost sensitivity for non-critical lint/test workloads. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and cache hints.

Security & compliance: must meet SOC2/ISO expectations, KMS-backed keys for signing artifacts, retention controls by workspace, and optional on-prem deployment for enterprise customers. Ask: proof of concept to demonstrate no-data-leakage during tool-calls (network egress disabled).

Quote from engineering lead: "If Redwood can stream build logs back to VSCode with <200ms tail latency while tests run in an isolated container, we can move from our existing in-house copilot."

POC scope (agreed): small repo with 20 tests, custom linter instrumented as a function-call, sandbox container image supplied by Emerald, test log streaming to ephemeral WebSocket, and automatic fallback to a smaller model for lint-only requests.

Decision criteria: security gating + demonstrable audit logs, memory/latency SLOs for streaming, CI throughput and cost per test token.
